setup: (fset 'my-when (if (fboundp 'defmacro) (cons 'macro (lambda (c b) (list 'if c b))) (macro (c b) (list 'if c b))))
note: 10B, the other half of the alias rule: the head is rewritten only when the alias target is itself a macro (Emacs' `(and (symbolp def) (macrop def))` in subr.el). `pf` aliases a plain function, so the form is left completely alone -- `(pf 1)`, not `(plain 1)`. Getting this wrong is invisible until someone aliases a function. The setup is dialect-neutral by construction: Emacs stores a macro as a `(macro . FUNCTION)` cons in the function cell and fe has a distinct macro object, so each transformer is installed through whichever spelling the running dialect has, selected by `(fboundp 'defmacro)` -- t in Emacs, nil in standalone fe. Nothing else about the case differs between the sides.
